strongest_alternative: The oral speaker may use attacks colloquially to mean animals harmed. The source and year are not expressly identified in that opening sentence, so the 2024 report attribution remains an inference. Nonetheless, the exact 91% sheep/goat pairing in the latest pre-hearing report, coupled with the later explicit DBBW 2024 protection-cost reference, makes the matched-source inference strong enough for a provisional minor finding. It is not proof that the speaker copied that chart or that every conceivable historical or local event share was different.
materiality: Minor: on the natural event-count reading the matched 2024 share is overstated by about 12 percentage points. Both 79% of attacks and 91% of harmed animals show a clear concentration on sheep/goats, so the central burden claim and practical request survive the correction.
direction: True only for the numerical concentration rationale: a larger apparent share of attack events strengthens the represented sector's urgent-removal argument. It does not prove that removal is effective or justified.
recommended_limits: Continue to call this a distinction in the matching 2024 report, not a proven current 2026 share.

Keep the lack of an explicit local source/year and oral-shorthand alternative prominent; use medium or qualified confidence for source identification, separately from high confidence in the primary chart distinction.
